sites_https_justification: The repository, npm and every documentation link are HTTPS only.
description_good_justification: README opening paragraph: provisioning users from Better Auth to the apps they use, over SCIM 2.0, Google Workspace and signed webhooks: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning#readme
interact_justification: How to get it (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/README.md#install), give feedback and report problems (GitHub issues, https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), and report vulnerabilities privately (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md — tests with every change (a bug fix includes the test that would have caught it), security checks mutation-checked, docs and a CHANGELOG entry with the code, Biome lint with --error-on-warnings and TypeScript strict as the coding standard, and pnpm typecheck, lint, test and pack:check must pass; CI enforces these on every pull request.
floss_license_justification: MIT, approved by the Open Source Initiative.
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT, approved by the Open Source Initiative.
documentation_basics_justification: The README covers install, setup, every target type, groups, what is sent, delivery and limits: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/README.md
documentation_interface_justification: The README documents every option, endpoint and event (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/README.md#set-up, https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/README.md#targets, https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/README.md#watching-it); exported TypeScript types; versioning in https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/docs/versioning.md
repo_track_justification: git on GitHub tracks every change, who made it and when.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands on main through a pull request, so the repository holds every interim version between releases, not only releases: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/commits/main and https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/pulls?q=is%3Apr. Releases are tags on main.
repo_distributed_justification: git, a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique semantic version in package.json, published once to npm (npm refuses to reuse a version) and tagged in git, e.g. 1.0.0: https://www.npmjs.com/package/better-auth-scim-provisioning?activeTab=versions and https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/releases
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, with what each part promises (including what an app receives) in https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/docs/versioning.md
version_tags_justification: Every release is a git tag vX.Y.Z on main, created by the tag-release workflow when the release pull request merges; the release workflow refuses a tag that doesn't match package.json or isn't on main: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/tags
release_notes_justification: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog); each GitHub release links its section.
release_notes_vulns_justification: A release that fixes a vulnerability says so in a Security section of the CHANGELOG and in a GitHub security advisory, with a CVE where one applies (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
report_process_justification: GitHub issues (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/issues) for bugs and app interop reports, as https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md describes; vulnerabilities privately (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
report_responses_justification: The maintainer responds to issues; https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/SECURITY.md sets a 7-day acknowledgement target for vulnerability reports.
enhancement_responses_justification: Feature requests through GitHub issues; the README's "Not yet" section records what is planned or declined: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/README.md#not-yet
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests are public, permanently archived and searchable: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/security/advisories/new (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
build_justification: pnpm build (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/scripts/build.mjs); CI builds and checks the package on every change (pnpm pack:check).
test_most_justification: About 300 tests in 80 files: unit and integration tests against a mock SCIM app, a mock Google Directory API and webhook receivers, concurrency and regression tests; the adapter matrix on Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB, Drizzle, Prisma and D1; the package on Workers; the example built in CI; live tests against Cloudflare Access, Google Workspace and AWS IAM Identity Center (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks).
test_policy_justification: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md: "Tests with every change. A bug fix comes with the test that would have caught it."
tests_are_added_justification: Each feature and fix pull request adds its tests; fixes from the independent review of the target registry came with failing-first tests (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/pull/58); regressions live in test/regressions/.
warnings_justification: TypeScript strict; Biome lint with --error-on-warnings in CI.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on lint warnings and type errors.
warnings_strict_justification: strict: true, and lint warnings are errors.
know_secure_design_justification: Credentials to apps are encrypted, bound to their target and organization, and never shown or sent anywhere new; app URLs must be https on the standard port and resolve to public addresses (checked before each request); an existing account is adopted only under strict rules; delivery survives outages through an outbox with leases (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/README.md#how-it-holds-up, https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/README.md#organizations-own-targets). An independent review of the target registry was fixed before merge (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/pull/58).
know_common_errors_justification: Server-side request forgery (https, public addresses, re-checked before each request), credential leaks (encrypted, never returned), account takeover through adoption (verified email only, nobody else's account), replayed or forged webhooks (HMAC-SHA256 signatures with a timestamp), and lost or duplicated changes under concurrency are addressed and tested (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/README.md).
crypto_published_justification: HMAC-SHA256 for webhook signatures, RS256 (RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 with SHA-256) for Google service-account sign-in, and Better Auth's symmetric encryption (XChaCha20-Poly1305) for stored credentials: all published, standard algorithms.
crypto_call_justification: WebCrypto (crypto.subtle) and Better Auth's symmetricEncrypt; no custom cryptographic primitives.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptography is implementable with FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: Google service-account keys are Google's RSA 2048-bit keys; HMAC keys are the host's secrets; stored credentials use 256-bit keys derived from Better Auth's secret.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithms are used or offered (no MD5, SHA-1 or DES).
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 or other algorithms with known serious weaknesses.
crypto_pfs_justification: The plugin doesn't implement network protocols itself; it calls apps over HTTPS, whose TLS (with forward secrecy) is the runtime's.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The plugin stores no user passwords; Better Auth does. Credentials to apps are stored encrypted, not hashed, because they must be sent.
crypto_random_justification: IDs and keys from crypto.randomUUID and crypto.getRandomValues (cryptographically secure).
delivery_mitm_justification: Delivered over HTTPS from npm and GitHub. Published only from CI with npm trusted publishing: SLSA provenance on npm, a Sigstore bundle and a CycloneDX SBOM on each GitHub release, and every version staged and approved by the maintainer (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is retrieved over HTTP.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No publicly known unpatched vulnerabilities; pnpm audit of the runtime dependencies runs on every push and pull request.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerabilities; the runtime audit blocks on any.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (security-extended) on every pull request and push to main (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml); Biome; TypeScript strict.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL alerts are fixed or dismissed with a recorded reason; a pull request that adds an alert fails.
static_analysis_often_justification: Every pull request and every push to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzing or sanitizer runs yet. Behaviour under failure is tested dynamically instead: mock apps that time out, throttle (429 with Retry-After), return errors and lag; concurrent deliveries across instances; and live tests against real services.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Failures found by the concurrency, adapter and live tests were fixed with regression tests (test/regressions/).
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions on every pull request and push to main (https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-scim-provisioning/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml): Better Auth at the peer range's minimum and the latest 1.7, Node 22 and 24, the adapter matrix, Workers runtimes, the example, gitleaks; plus CodeQL and dependency audits.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests: searchable, addressable by URL, open to new participants.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: gitleaks scans the full history in CI; tests use mock services and throwaway credentials; live-test settings stay in a git-ignored file.
maintained_justification: Actively developed: 1.0.0 released 2026-10-06; see the commit history.
